column1: # Hoist sail and steer under a Calm wind.
# `weather.md §5`: "Calm wind never releases a cached hoisted-sail
# movement. The ship waits until the player enters a different command. A
# later Pass command reports the stalled-sailing feedback `Sheets in
# irons!\n` and clears the cached sailing state. That Pass adds no ordinary
# `Pass` echo. The unsuccessful unchanged-heading attempt itself adds no
# stalled-sailing sentence." The first heading key only sets the cache
# (`§5.1`: a heading that differs from the cache turns and does not move).
# Lead from #45: in an earlier drowning-collision run the stock game showed
# no direction echo 0.7 s after a heading key while its wind had drifted to
# Calm, where this engine echoed at once - but this engine's wind was East
# then, so the two were not comparable. Here both sides start Calm.
# The wind drifts on its own (`weather.md` "Autonomous Wind Drift", a 1-in-64
# roll per world tick), so the opening waits are kept short and the `start`
# and `pass` shots both show the banner: a run where either side's banner
# has left Calm measured something else. The opening waits match
# drowning-collision's, which a loaded host needs to get the stock game past
# its title menu.
# Wind lottery, measured 2026-10-16 over six runs with this seed and these
# keys: the stock side's `start` banner read North, Calm, South, South and
# East (the sixth run never left the title), and within one run it went from
# Calm at `start` to West at `hoisted`, 1.5 s later; the engine side read East,
# West, East, Calm and West. Neither side holds the seed's Calm byte through
# the opening waits, so a run is only comparable where both banners agree at
# `hoisted`, and the Calm premise itself has not yet been measured. What the
# non-Calm runs do measure: stock prints `>Yell HOIST!` / blank /
# `>BREAKING UP!` when the key's step is refused on the same command - the
# refusal is written on the marker row the prompt drew before the
# (echo-less) hoisted key.
# The `pass` beat lands in the drowning loop, whose passes each draw `1..8`
# per member (`vehicles.md` Section 6), so the Avatar's hit points in the panel
# are a roll on both sides. Until 2026-10-24 the engine read `0D` there on
# every run: its passes held for the damage rumble alone and the loop was over
# about 1.3 s after `DROWNING!!!`. With the impact rumble on every pass both
# sides are mid-loop at `pass` (20261024-012310: every message-window beat
# agrees; the panel reads the two sides' rolls).
# requires-seed: profile `seed-sail-calm` (seed-drowning-collision with the wind byte set to Calm)
